content.text:
I changed `lib/adapters/http.js` (around line 280) so that the default `maxBodyLength` is unlimited whether or not redirects are followed. I haven't run any tests or tried the issue's repro since the change.

**Cause:** axios's default `maxBodyLength` is `-1`, meaning no limit. The HTTP adapter only passed the option to `follow-redirects` when it was greater than `-1`. So when the option was left at its default (or set to `-1` explicitly), `follow-redirects` used its own 10MB limit. With `maxRedirects: 0` that library isn't used at all, which is why there was no limit in that case.

**Fix:** when `maxBodyLength` is `-1` or lower, the adapter now passes `Infinity` to `follow-redirects`. A positive value you set yourself is still passed through and enforced as before.

This one change addresses the behaviour in the issue. The README's `maxBodyLength` entry still doesn't say what the default is; adding a `// default: -1 (unlimited)` note there would cover the documentation point if you want it.
